title: Let a team of agents develop testable research ideas
summary: Researchers built DiscoveryRSI, where agents grow and revise life-science hypotheses into experiment plans; they report their 27B model compiled 50% more runnable tasks than its base.
agent_role: Agents propose hypotheses, add controls and evidence, revise them over rounds, and turn chosen ones into runnable computational tasks; experts must review the output.
outcome: The authors report DiscoveryRSI-27B selected 16.7% more unique hypotheses and compiled 50% more tasks than its base model in matched runs.
what_they_did: A research team built a system where several agents propose research hypotheses in life science. Each idea carries evidence, a plan and rules for disproving it. The agents revise ideas over rounds and turn some into runnable computer experiments. They also trained a 27B model on this research experience and run a live public demo.
how_it_went: The authors report their model had the highest rate of usable references in their comparison, at 6.3%. They say it picked 16.7% more unique hypotheses and compiled 50% more tasks than its base model.
worth_knowing: The authors warn it can produce plausible but unsupported claims or infeasible experiments, so every hypothesis needs expert review and checking.
prompt: Help me develop research hypotheses on [research question] in [field]. For each, write a clear claim backed by sources, a plan to test it, what result would prove it wrong, and alternative explanations. Then critique each one, add missing controls or measurements, and revise. Keep a record of how each idea changed and why. Use only data I provide: [dataset or sources]. Show me the ranked list with sources before going further, and flag anything you are unsure of.

curation.rationale: A real multi-agent research workflow for life-science hypotheses with a paper, code, live demo and comparison numbers, though it reads mostly as a model and framework release with benchmark-style results.
